_comment: Published translated titles for the 30 public-domain classics, applied by
These are the titles the books were actually published under in each language,
not translations of the English title. Machine translation gets them wrong in a
way that is invisible unless you know the book: LibreTranslate rendered Just So
Stories as 'Juste pour des histoires' (published: 'Histoires comme ca'), White
Fang as 'Fang blanc' (published: 'Croc-Blanc'), and Twenty Thousand Leagues as
'Vingt mille ligues' - 'ligues' being alliances, where Verne wrote 'lieues', the
A title identical to English is deliberate where the book is published under the
original name (Heidi, Peter Pan, Robinson Crusoe, Oliver Twist). tools/audit_titles.py
treats those as intentional and only reports the rest.

titles._picture_books: Not classics - these are CC-licensed picture books whose titles the machine could not handle. LibreTranslate passes through short title-case fragments with no terminal punctuation ('Cat Dreams' comes back as 'Cat Dreams'), and half-translates the rest ('Gordo rey Thin perro'), so these few are set by hand.

cover_force_generated: _comment: Commons has real art for these, but not art that works as a cover. gb76 is a photograph of the bound book with the spine in frame, so cropping to 2:3 slices the title off the fore-edge; gb2781 is the 'This is my book' bookplate from inside the front cover. No automatic check catches either - they are detailed, correctly-matched images that simply are not covers.

identical_ok._comment: Titles that are correctly the same as English, so the audit stops flagging them. 'Wind' is the German word for wind; 'Tita' is a character's name.
